0001: Title of the solution.
0002: Begins the claim statement.
0003: States the LongPath17 decision problem.
0004: Claims the problem is NP-hard and in NP.
0005: Justifies NP membership.
0006: Introduces reduction from Hamiltonian Path.
0007: Defines Hamiltonian path.
0008: States Hamiltonian Path is NP-complete.
0009: Cites standard references for Hamiltonian Path.
0010: States intent to show a reduction to LongPath17.
0011: Takes an arbitrary instance H of Hamiltonian Path.
0012: Begins construction of instance G for LongPath17.
0013: Initializes G as a copy of H.
0014: Adds 17 new isolated vertices to G.
0015: Defines the final vertex and edge sets of G.
0016: Reiterates that no new edges are added.
0017: Notes the construction is polynomial-time.
0018: States G has n+17 vertices.
0019: States the bidirectional claim for the reduction.
0020: Begins the forward direction proof.
0021: Assumes H has a Hamiltonian path PH.
0022: Considers PH as a path in G.
0023: States PH is a valid path in G because G contains H.
0024: Notes PH visits all n original vertices.
0025: Notes PH does not visit any isolated vertices.
0026: Concludes PH is a simple path in G.
0027: Calculates that PH visits |VG|-17 vertices.
0028: Concludes G has a valid simple path.
0029: Begins the reverse direction proof.
0030: Assumes G has a simple path PG visiting |VG|-17 vertices.
0031: Substitutes |VG| = n+17 to show PG visits n vertices.
0032: States PG visits n distinct vertices of G.
0033: Flawed step: logically invalid claim that any set of n vertices chosen from G (which has n+17 vertices) must include all n original vertices of VH.
0034: Continues the flawed reasoning by claiming such a size-n set could also contain added vertices, which is impossible.
0035: Argues correctly that PG cannot include isolated vertices if it's connected and n>1.
0036: Explains isolated vertices have no edges.
0037: Explains a path would get stuck at an isolated vertex.
0038: Notes an isolated vertex only forms a path of length 0 (1 vertex).
0039: Concludes PG cannot visit isolated vertices (assuming n>1).
0040: Formalizes the connected component argument.
0041: Notes PG must lie entirely in the connected component of H.
0042: Notes isolated vertices are in separate components.
0043: Page number.
0044: Blank line.
0045: Concludes PG must visit n vertices entirely from VH.
0046: Concludes PG restricted to VH is a Hamiltonian path of H.
0047: Justifies that edges of PG are in EH.
0048: Reaffirms the restriction is a valid path in H.
0049: Concludes H has a Hamiltonian path.
0050: Summarizes the iff equivalence.
0051: Recalls the transformation is computable in polynomial time.
0052: Concludes this is a valid polynomial-time reduction.
0053: Concludes LongPath17 is NP-hard.
0054: Concludes LongPath17 is NP-complete.
